## 5. Non-Obvious Pattern

**WOLF achieved perfect operational availability with zero operational output — and the system worked exactly as designed.**

50 commits in 4 hours and 7 minutes. No missed intervals. No drift. The telemetry pipeline is rock-solid. But every single commit was a read-only observation of a portfolio that couldn't be touched.

The interesting thing is what this reveals about the circuit breaker design: it's a protection mechanism that fires once and then *stays fired* for the rest of the trading day regardless of what happens to the portfolio. So when TSLA dropped hard and PLTR/MSFT/NVDA softened, WOLF watched the loss deepen from -5.2% to -6.7% with no mechanism to rebalance, hedge, or reduce. The CB protects against WOLF making things *worse* but also prevents WOLF from making things *better*.

This is a design choice worth surfacing: **the CB currently only has a "halt entries" lever, not a "reduce risk" lever.** A second mode — say, CB yellow = no new entries but allow position reduction — would give WOLF one more degree of freedom when the circuit fires. Today's session is the clearest possible argument for that addition.

Cross-cutting: the same pattern shows up in the agent silence. Every agent that isn't logging to PRAXIS is also in a kind of "CB-locked" state — present, potentially running, but producing no observable output. The Construct can't act on signals it can't see.
